content:
The **2014–15 Missouri State Lady Bears basketball team** represented Missouri State University (then known as Missouri State University–Springfield) during the **2014–15 NCAA Division I women's basketball season**. The team competed in the **Missouri Valley Conference (MVC)** and was led by **head coach Kellie Harper**, who was in her **third and final season** at Missouri State before departing for Washington State.

Here’s a detailed breakdown of the team’s season:

---

### **Key Details**
- **Head Coach**: Kellie Harper (3rd season, 45–48 record at MSU)
- **Conference**: Missouri Valley Conference (MVC)
- **Arena**: JQH Arena (Capacity: 11,000)
- **Record**:
  - **Overall**: 19–14
  - **Conference**: 11–7 (Tied for 3rd in MVC)
  - **Postseason**: **WNIT Second Round**
- **Final Rankings**: Unranked in AP/Coaches Poll

---

### **Preseason Outlook**
- The Lady Bears were picked to finish **4th in the MVC preseason poll** (behind Wichita State, Northern Iowa, and Drake).
- Returning starters included **Tyonna Snow** (Sr., G) and **Liza Fruendt** (Jr., F), while **Karly Buer** (So., G) and **Lexi Hughes** (Jr., G) were expected to contribute heavily.
- The team aimed to improve after a **14–17 (7–11 MVC) record in 2013–14** and a first-round exit in the MVC Tournament.

---

### **Roster & Key Players**
| **Player**          | **Pos.** | **Yr.** | **PPG** | **RPG** | **APG** | **Notes** |
|----------------------|----------|---------|---------|---------|---------|-----------|
| **Tyonna Snow**      | G        | Sr.     | 14.3    | 3.5     | 2.8     | **1st Team All-MVC**, led team in scoring |
| **Liza Fruendt**     | F        | Jr.     | 12.1    | 6.8     | 1.5     | **2nd Team All-MVC**, led in rebounding |
| **Karly Buer**       | G        | So.     | 9.8     | 2.9     | 2.1     | Key perimeter shooter |
| **Lexi Hughes**      | G        | Jr.     | 8.7     | 3.1     | 1.8     | Strong defender, 3PT threat |
| **Maryam Dembele**   | F        | Sr.     | 6.2     | 5.4     | 0.5     | Physical presence in the paint |
| **Audrey Holt**      | F        | Fr.     | 5.1     | 4.2     | 0.3     | Future star (later MVC Player of the Year) |

**Other Contributors**:
- **Danielle Gitthens** (Fr., G) – Emerging scorer off the bench.
- **Jasmine Johnson** (Sr., G) – Veteran leadership.

---

### **Season Summary**
#### **Non-Conference (8–5)**
- **Notable Wins**:
  - **vs. Arkansas (68–63)** – Upset SEC opponent at home (Nov. 23).
  - **vs. Oral Roberts (71–66)** – Road win over Summit League foe.
- **Notable Losses**:
  - **vs. Oklahoma (56–78)** – Struggled against Big 12 power.
  - **vs. Kansas State (50–63)** – Tough road loss.
- **Key Takeaway**: The team showed resilience, including a **5-game win streak** in December.

#### **Conference Play (11–7, T-3rd in MVC)**
- **Best Wins**:
  - **vs. Wichita State (65–59, Jan. 23)** – Snapped Shockers’ 12-game MVC win streak.
  - **vs. Northern Iowa (68–61, Feb. 13)** – Swept season series vs. Panthers.
- **Tough Losses**:
  - **vs. Drake (58–64, Jan. 9)** – Close loss to eventual MVC champs.
  - **vs. Illinois State (60–65, Feb. 27)** – Late-season setback.
- **Standings**:
  - **Drake (15–3)** won the MVC, followed by **Northern Iowa (14–4)** and **Wichita State (13–5)**. Missouri State tied for **3rd (11–7)**.

#### **MVC Tournament (March 12–15, 2015 – St. Charles, MO)**
- **Quarterfinals**: **Missouri State 70, Loyola (IL) 56** – Snow (22 pts) led the way.
- **Semifinals**: **Missouri State 65, Northern Iowa 60** – Fruendt (18 pts, 12 reb) dominated.
- **Championship**: **Drake 74, Missouri State 65** – Lady Bears fell short despite Snow’s 21 pts.

**Result**: **Runner-up** (automatic bid to **WNIT**).

---
### **Postseason: WNIT (Women’s National Invitation Tournament)**
- **First Round (March 19)**: **Missouri State 78, Oral Roberts 68** – Snow (24 pts), Fruendt (16 pts, 13 reb).
- **Second Round (March 22)**: **Missouri State 63, Colorado 70** – Season ended in Boulder.

---
### **Season Highlights & Awards**
- **Tyonna Snow**:
  - **1st Team All-MVC**
  - **MVC Tournament MVP** (averaged 22.3 PPG in tournament)
  - Finished career **6th in MSU history in scoring (1,500+ pts)**.
- **Liza Fruendt**:
  - **2nd Team All-MVC**
  - **MVC All-Tournament Team**
  - Led MVC in **double-doubles (12)**.
- **Team Accolades**:
  - **Most MVC wins (11) since 2006–07**.
  - **First postseason berth since 2011** (WNIT).
  - **Defeated 3 eventual NCAA Tournament teams** (Arkansas, Wichita State, Northern Iowa).

---
### **Statistical Leaders (2014–15)**
| **Category**       | **Player**      | **Stat** |
|--------------------|-----------------|----------|
| **Points**         | Tyonna Snow     | 14.3 PPG |
| **Rebounds**       | Liza Fruendt    | 6.8 RPG  |
| **Assists**        | Tyonna Snow     | 2.8 APG  |
| **Steals**         | Lexi Hughes     | 1.6 SPG  |
| **Blocks**         | Maryam Dembele  | 0.9 BPG  |
| **3PT %**          | Karly Buer      | 38.5%    |
| **FG %**           | Liza Fruendt    | 48.1%    |

---
### **Aftermath & Legacy**
- **Coaching Change**: Kellie Harper left for **Washington State** after the season (hired as head coach).
- **New Coach**: **Katie Abrahamson-Henderson** (formerly of Albany) was hired in April 2015 but **left after one season** for Central Michigan.
- **Player Developments**:
  - **Audrey Holt** became a **star** under new coaches, earning **MVC Player of the Year (2016–17)**.
  - **Danielle Gitthens** later transferred to **Kansas State**.
- **Program Direction**: The 2014–15 season marked a **turnaround** after struggles in Harper’s first two years, setting the stage for future success under **Kellie Harper’s recruits**.

---
### **Notable Games (Full Schedule Highlights)**
| **Date**       | **Opponent**          | **Result**       | **Key Notes** |
|----------------|-----------------------|------------------|---------------|
| Nov. 23, 2014  | Arkansas              | **W 68–63**      | Upset SEC team |
| Jan. 23, 2015  | Wichita State         | **W 65–59**      | Ended Shockers’ streak |
| Feb. 13, 2015  | Northern Iowa         | **W 68–61**      | Swept Panthers |
| Mar. 15, 2015  | Drake (MVC Final)     | **L 65–74**      | Snow’s 21 pts |
| Mar. 22, 2015  | Colorado (WNIT)       | **L 63–70**      | Season finale |

---
### **Conclusion**
The **2014–15 Missouri State Lady Bears** were a **gritty, overachieving team** that exceeded expectations by:
- Finishing **3rd in the MVC** (up from 7th the prior year).
- Reaching the **MVC Tournament final** and **WNIT Second Round**.
- Featuring **two All-MVC players (Snow & Fruendt)** and a **future star in Audrey Holt**.

While they fell short of an NCAA Tournament bid, the season **re-established Missouri State as a MVC contender** and provided momentum for future success.
